horizontal_overflow_detail.root_cause: Unwrapped long claim_id strings (e.g. '57d7b4c4-...:trader:trader_investment_plan:claim:X') rendered inside <code> elements in the Analyst findings panel (and similarly in AlphaCard's own evidence claim-id text) have no overflow-wrap/word-break CSS rule, so they render at full intrinsic width and push the page wider than the 768px viewport (confirmed: scrollWidth 866px vs 768px viewport).
horizontal_overflow_detail.note: This is the ONLY horizontal-overflow finding in the entire rehearsal; it does not occur at the planned 1440x900 desktop demo width.

small_viewport_sanity_pass.result: MATERIAL_NONBLOCKER -- does not affect the planned desktop demo, but is a genuine layout defect at narrow width

browser_console_and_network.console_warnings_breakdown: 100% React Router 'future flag' deprecation notices (v7_startTransition / v7_relativeSplatPath) -- framework-level, not application-logic warnings, invisible to a normal demo audience (DevTools not open during a stakeholder demo)
browser_console_and_network.failed_network_requests_root_cause: 100% net::ERR_ABORTED, caused by the rehearsal script's own rapid, automated page-to-page navigation cancelling in-flight AbortController-based requests (e.g. status polling, graph/conflict fetches) via each page's own unmount cleanup -- this is the application's intentional, already-tested cancellation-safety behavior (confirmed throughout Phase 1-2D), not a genuine request failure a human presenter clicking at normal pace would meaningfully reproduce or notice.
browser_console_and_network.disclosure_note: Disclosed in full per task instruction not to declare readiness without disclosing recurring console/network activity, even though root-cause analysis attributes both findings to (1) benign framework deprecation notices and (2) the rehearsal script's own navigation speed rather than a product defect.

load_time_measurement.methodology_note: An initial measurement pass using Playwright's 'networkidle' wait condition produced misleadingly high figures (~16 seconds) for several pages. Investigation confirmed this was an artifact of the Vite dev server's persistent HMR WebSocket connection preventing true network idle, NOT real user-perceived latency. A corrected, content-based measurement (time until the actual first-screen content -- e.g. 'Structural snapshot' -- appears in the DOM) was used instead and is reported below.
load_time_measurement.note: All measured pages render their core content in well under one second against the already-persisted real data -- effectively immediate for a persisted-run demo.

findings.page: ResearchRunPage.tsx (Analyst findings panel) and AlphaCard.tsx (evidence claim-id)
findings.component: FindingCard's claim-id <code> element; AlphaCard's evidence claim-id <code> element
findings.steps_to_reproduce: Open any persisted run's Research page (confirmed on NVDA/QQQ/SNDK) at a 768px-wide viewport and check document.documentElement.scrollWidth vs clientWidth.
findings.expected_behavior: No horizontal page overflow at the existing 768px breakpoint (per the project's own established responsive convention).
findings.actual_behavior: Long, unbroken claim_id strings (e.g. '57d7b4c4-...:trader:trader_investment_plan:claim:5') render inside <code> elements with no overflow-wrap/word-break rule, pushing page scrollWidth to 866px against a 768px viewport -- a real, confirmed (screenshot-verified) horizontal scrollbar.
findings.likely_scope: Small, presentation-only CSS fix (add overflow-wrap/word-break to the relevant <code> selectors) -- not attempted in this phase per the read-only mandate.

findings.steps_to_reproduce: Open browser DevTools console while navigating any route.
findings.actual_behavior: 26 React Router v7 'future flag' deprecation warnings observed across the rehearsal -- framework-level, non-application-logic, invisible to a normal demo audience.
findings.likely_scope: Trivial -- add the two future-flag opt-ins to the router config, or ignore until a React Router v7 upgrade.

findings.steps_to_reproduce: Navigate rapidly between pages via an automated script.
findings.expected_behavior: N/A -- this is not a product finding.
findings.actual_behavior: 24 net::ERR_ABORTED network events recorded, all attributable to the app's own intentional AbortController-based request-cancellation-on-unmount behavior being triggered by the rehearsal script's faster-than-human navigation speed, not a real product defect.
findings.likely_scope: No action needed -- documented for completeness per the task's disclosure instruction.
